messages.subject: SE.type =  'BL', 'SEM'
parts:
Hi Phil,
Thanks again for putting together such great software and maintaining it so well - this is such a life-saver for grad students in psychometrics. 

Two (hopefully quick) questions about standard errors in your MIRT package.

1. SE.type = 'BL' : the numerical approximation of the observed Hessian - why are you calling it the Bock and Lieberman approach? I don't see anything about it in their 1970 manuscript. Was this a typo? Do you know who else has done any work with numerical approximations to find SEs? 

2. SE.type = 'SEM' , technical=list('symmetric_SEM' = FALSE) - where do you apply the forceSymmetric() ?
I looked here but can't find it. https://github.com/philchalmers/mirt/blob/master/R/SE.methods.R

Hope these are reasonable questions. I look forward to hearing from you.
Thanks for your time,
Charlie

On Thu, Sep 17, 2015 at 3:37 PM, Charlie_Rutgers <charles.i...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Phil,
Thanks again for putting together such great software and maintaining it so well - this is such a life-saver for grad students in psychometrics. 

Two (hopefully quick) questions about standard errors in your MIRT package.

1. SE.type = 'BL' : the numerical approximation of the observed Hessian - why are you calling it the Bock and Lieberman approach? I don't see anything about it in their 1970 manuscript. Was this a typo? Do you know who else has done any work with numerical approximations to find SEs?

It's the Hessian of the observed log-likelihood equations, which is what Bock and Leiberman describe in their optimization process. I don't evaluate it analytically, but instead use a high-precision numerical approximation to build the elements. There as a paper by Tian et al (2012) in EPM that talks about other methods as well I believe.

2. SE.type = 'SEM' , technical=list('symmetric_SEM' = FALSE) - where do you apply the forceSymmetric() ?
I looked here but can't find it. https://github.com/philchalmers/mirt/blob/master/R/SE.methods.R

Check the 03-estimation.R function, which is really the main workflow of the package. The S-EM function has to be called many times to scrape different aspects of the observed data log-likelihood, so the file you point to is just in reference to the function that has to be called numerous times. Forcing it to be symmetric is one trick I've added to help the information matrix be more stable (S-EM is surprisingly unstable at times, so it needs all the help it can get). Cheers.

Phil

Hope these are reasonable questions. I look forward to hearing from you.
Thanks for your time,
Charlie
